angle_en: Avyakta, the unmanifest, is the source of his visible form
angle_hi: अव्यक्त, जो अदृश्य है, उनके रूप का स्रोत है

en.intro: Krishna asks you to listen for one word that describes the true source of his human form.
en.notice: The unwise think I have taken a visible form from the unseen. They do not know that avyakta, the unmanifest, is the source from which this visible form came.
en.next: Krishna then explains that he is hidden from the deluded by yoga-maya, his divine illusion.
en.meaning: The unwise think I have taken a visible form from the unseen. They do not know my imperishable, supreme nature.

hi.intro: कृष्ण आपसे एक शब्द सुनने के लिए कहते हैं, जो उनके मानव रूप के असली स्रोत को बताता है।
hi.meaning: बुद्धिहीन मनुष्य मेरे सर्वश्रेष्ठ अविनाशी परमभावको न जानते हुए, अव्यक्त से दृश्य रूप धारण करने वाले मुझको मनुष्य की तरह ही शरीर धारण करनेवाला मानते हैं ॥
hi.notice: अबुद्धयः, यानी बुद्धिहीन लोग, यह मानते हैं कि मैंने अव्यक्त से दृश्य रूप धारण किया है। वे यह नहीं जानते कि अव्यक्त से यह रूप आया है, और वे मेरे अव्यय और अनुत्तम भाव को नहीं जानते।
hi.next: कृष्ण आगे कहते हैं कि वे माया से ढके हैं, इसलिए सब उन्हें नहीं देख पाते।

issues: meaning_changed: "बुद्धिहीन मनुष्य मेरे सर्वश्रेष्ठ अविनाशी परमभावको न जानते हुए अव्यक्त मनइन्द्रियोंसे पर मुझ सच्चिदानन्दघन परमात्माको मनुष्यकी तरह ही शरीर धारण करनेवाला मानते हैं ॥" (The Hindi meaning changes the source of the visible form. The English meaning says the unwise think the unmanifest has taken a visible form ('taken a visible form from the unseen'). The Hindi incorrectly inserts 'मनइन्द्रियोंसे' (by the mind and senses) and presents 'अव्यक्त' as a separate object, implying they see the unmanifest through the mind and senses, rather than thinking the unmanifest has taken a form.)

unsupported: "सच्चिदानन्दघन परमात्माको" (The term 'सच्चिदानन्दघन परमात्मा' (the embodiment of truth, consciousness, and bliss) is not found in the verse's word meanings or the provided English/Hindi translation, and is not supported by the source.)

meaning_changed: "बुद्धिहीन मनुष्य मेरे सर्वश्रेष्ठ अविनाशी परमभावको न जानते हुए अव्यक्त को मन और इन्द्रियों से पर मुझ सच्चिदानन्दघन परमात्माको मनुष्य की तरह ही शरीर धारण करनेवाला मानते हैं ॥" (The Hindi meaning incorrectly states that the unwise 'think the unmanifest (avyakta) with the mind and senses', which drops and contradicts the original Sanskrit 'manvanti mam abuddhayah' (the unwise think of me as having a manifest form) and 'param bhāvam ajānanto' (not knowing my supreme nature). It also adds 'sacchidānandaghana parameshvara' (dense embodiment of consciousness-bliss-supreme lord) which is not in the source.)

meaning_changed: "बुद्धिहीन मनुष्य मेरे सर्वश्रेष्ठ अविनाशी परमभावको न जानते हुए अव्यक्त से व्यक्ति रूप प्राप्त करने वाले मुझको मनुष्य की तरह ही शरीर धारण करनेवाला मानते हैं ॥" (The Hindi meaning introduces the phrase 'अव्यक्त से व्यक्ति रूप प्राप्त करने वाले' (having obtained a manifest form from the unmanifest), which is not present in the Sanskrit source or the English meaning. The source only states they think he has taken a visible form from the unseen; it does not explicitly state that they think he 'obtained' it from the unmanifest.)

meaning_changed: "अबुद्धयः, यानी बुद्धिहीन लोग, केवल एक शरीर देखते हैं।" (The English meaning states the unwise think he has 'taken a visible form from the unseen'. The Hindi notice claims they 'only see one body' (केवल एक शरीर देखते हैं), which drops the crucial element of them thinking he has taken a form from the unseen, softening the meaning.)
